condition: rough scaly sun damaged actinic spots on bald scalp over several months
level_rationale: Four rough spots on the bald scalp of a 72-year-old adult who gardens outdoors that have stayed scaly and red for 5 months describe persistent chronic sun-exposed keratotic scalp lesions warranting an outpatient physician skin examination, targeted lesion-directed or field therapy, and exclusion of cutaneous malignancy rather than unguided self-care or emergency care, whereas mild warmth on that bald scalp yesterday evening after outdoor gardening that subsided overnight represents harmless transient solar warmth needing only routine self-care.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 72 with a bald scalp, outdoor gardening, and 4 rough scalp spots staying scaly and red for 5 months without naming actinic keratosis, with an exact 0-word span difference (20 vs 20 words). Overriding plan.json's face/eye cellulitis plus rigors bundle under Rule A first choice, Rule D, and G4 site parity, replacing f3 at the exact same scalp site with mild evening scalp warmth that subsided overnight stays inside the outdoor-gardening bald-scalp case and shifts care cleanly from doctor evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
